content.intro: Modern PHP offers stronger type declarations and language constructs for making intent explicit. Choose the narrowest useful type and use enums, attributes, and readonly design only when they model a real rule. In this lesson, focus on intersection types; then compare it with combined union and intersection requirements. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use intersection and disjunctive normal form types when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Intersection and Disjunctive Normal Form Types
content_blocks.code:
<?php
final class Tax { public function amount(int $price): int { return intdiv($price, 10); } }
final class Checkout { public function __construct(private Tax $tax) {} public function total(int $price): int { return $price + $this->tax->amount($price); } }
echo (new Checkout(new Tax()))->total(100) . PHP_EOL;
